I can't see the figure, so I'm assuming the bar is a single strip of 10 triangles, each sharing an edge with the next (like a Toblerone bar).

In that case there are 9 interior edges between consecutive triangles. Each edge is either cut or left intact, giving $2^9 = 512$ divisions. Every cut set yields contiguous pieces, since the pieces are the runs between cuts along the strip. The only division excluded is the uncut bar, which has one piece, leaving $512 - 1 = 511$ divisions into two or more pieces.

If the actual figure is a different arrangement of triangles, the count would change.

ANSWER: 511
